recall.question: How is 'Reality' defined, specifically when distinguishing it from something that is merely apparent?
recall.answer: Reality is the state or quality of being real, meaning it exists independently of any ideas concerning it. It constitutes an actual thing.

recall.question: What are the three essential characteristics a system must satisfy to be classified as a Virtual Reality system?
recall.answer: A system must feature a virtual environment, provide an immersive experience, and be interactive in nature.

recall.question: Based on the prior lectures, how is something described as 'Virtual' in relation to factual existence?
recall.answer: Virtual is defined as existing in essence or effect, but not in fact. It is something that can be there but cannot be attributed to factual existence.

recall.question: Describe the dynamic nature of 'Interaction' within a virtual environment.
recall.answer: Interaction is a dynamic relationship where a user's actions or inputs cause measurable changes to the elements or content within the virtual environment.

quiz.stem: Which combination of features is essential for a system to be correctly classified as augmented reality?
options: It only needs to be able to combine virtual elements, provided the visual elements are enhanced.
It must be generated entirely by computer technology and perfectly simulate the real world environment.
It must combine real and virtual elements, allow for real-time interaction, and be registered in three dimensions (3D).
It must simply overlay digital information onto the real world without requiring any interaction.
explanations: The requirement is the combination of real and virtual input; simply enhancing the visual is not sufficient.
While technology creates the enhancement, AR systems are meant to enhance reality, not entirely simulate it.
An AR system requires all three defined characteristics: merging real and virtual reality, allowing for immediate interaction, and existing within a 3D space.
The definition specifies that the system must be interactive, meaning the user must be able to affect the digital overlay.

item.stem: Digital augmentations in marker-based AR are triggered and displayed only when the device is aimed directly at a recognized marker.
explanations: Marker-based systems require the device to detect a marker to know where and when to place the digital content.
Augmentations can be placed anywhere in the environment regardless of whether a marker is visible or detected.

recap.text: Augmented reality is defined as an enhanced version of our physical reality, achieved by using technology to layer digital information over what we are viewing. To qualify as an AR system, this overlay must seamlessly combine real and virtual content, allow the user to interact with the added digital elements instantly, and be presented in three dimensions.

review.question: How does augmented reality use technology to enhance reality?
review.answer: It uses technology, specifically computer systems, to overlay digital information onto an image of something that is being viewed through a device.

quiz.stem: For a digital enhancement to be considered part of a proper AR system, it must be registered in 3D space.
explanations: 3D registration ensures the digital content appears appropriately placed and seamlessly mixes with real-world objects.
If the content is not registered in 3D, it would appear randomly on the device, breaking the illusion.

quiz.stem: Must a user be able to interact with the digital content only when it is displayed separately from the enhanced environment?
explanations: If interaction occurs separately, the user loses the cohesive feeling of being immersed in the enhanced reality.
The system must support interaction with the digital content *within* the enhanced environment to maintain the feeling of being in reality.

recap.text: Augmented Reality fundamentally enhances the real world by blending computer-generated information with live imagery. For this blend to be effective, the digital additions must be precisely situated in three-dimensional space, and the user must be able to interact with these enhancements within the environment. Ultimately, all four characteristics—enhancement, 3D placement, sensory experience, and interaction—must be met to qualify as an AR system.

review.question: If a system satisfies three of the four required characteristics of an AR system, can it still be classified as AR?
review.answer: No. To be definitively called an AR system, all four characteristics must be fully satisfied. If even one element is missing or insufficient, the system does not meet the complete definition.

quiz.stem: What is the defining characteristic of a Virtual Reality (VR) system?
options: It only adds digital objects onto an existing real-world scene for context.
It modifies the ongoing sensory input of the user without fully obscuring reality.
It allows the user to observe the real world while occasionally adding digital enhancements.
It entirely replaces the user's real-world perception with a simulated digital environment.
explanations: This describes Augmented Reality (AR) because AR adds digital objects onto the real world.
This describes Augmented Reality (AR) because AR merely alters perception rather than replacing it entirely.
This describes Augmented Reality (AR) because AR keeps the real world visible while adding enhancements.
VR is defined by the fact that it substitutes the user's sense of reality completely with a virtual one.

recap.text: Augmented Reality alters how we perceive the real world by overlaying digital content onto existing physical environments. In contrast, Virtual Reality completely swaps out the real world for a wholly simulated digital environment. A key distinction is that AR requires a real-world setting to operate, whereas VR can create its own self-contained space.

review.question: How does Augmented Reality (AR) modify a user's perception of reality?
review.answer: AR alters perception by placing digital content onto a real-world view. This process, known as superimposition, allows digital elements to appear in physical locations.

quiz.stem: Any environment that is purely physical reality without the addition of any digital computer-generated content falls within the broader definition of Mixed Reality.
explanations: The definition describes the extreme ends of the continuum, not the space between them.
The definition places MR between the purely real environment and the purely virtual environment.

recap.text: Mixed Reality lacks a single, definitive definition, leading to various conceptual frameworks across the research community. Conceptually, MR occupies the space between a completely real world and a fully synthetic virtual world. From a technical perspective, many developers define MR as the capability of a device or application to successfully integrate both Augmented Reality and Virtual Reality functions.

review.question: How does the definition of MR as 'the combination of AR and VR' differ from the definition of MR as 'everything in between'?
review.answer: The 'everything in between' definition is broad, describing the spatial position on the continuum; the combination definition is specific to the technical capability of an application or device to merge both AR and VR functions.

recap.text: VR technologies provide an experience that completely replaces the user's existing perception of reality. Conversely, AR systems work by adding or enhancing elements to the user's real-world view. To simplify the discussion, many professionals treat Mixed Reality (MR) as being synonymous with AR.

review.question: What assumption regarding Mixed Reality (MR) and Augmented Reality (AR) is shared by many practitioners in the field?
review.answer: Many practitioners share the assumption that AR and MR refer to the same technology and idea.
